sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
sources.evidence: April 23, 2026 announcement explicitly releases GPT-5.5 Pro to eligible ChatGPT plans. An April 24 update adds API availability. Exact Pro benchmark columns establish the distinct Pro setting and performance, not numerical parameters.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 Pro API model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model document identifies the April 23 snapshot, 1,050,000 context, 128,000 maximum output, text/image input, text output, reasoning tokens, medium/high(default)/xhigh effort, Responses and Batch support, and function calling. It states no cached-input discount; lack of a caching feature flag is not a structural disclosure.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Introduction explicitly states GPT-5.5 Pro is the same underlying GPT-5.5 model with parallel test-time compute. Section 2 describes training; separate Pro evaluations account for behavioral differences. Complete extracted text gives no total/active production count or detailed network topology.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Later July 9 card contains exact gpt-5.5-pro columns in Tables 2 and 3 for protein binding and DNA sequence design. These are evaluation scores, not total/active parameter counts. Full document inspection found no parameter disclosure for this exact model; NanoGPT training tasks concern another small model.

sources.title: GeneBench: Assessing AI Agents for Multi-Stage Inference Problems in Genomics and Quantitative Biology
sources.evidence: Exact GPT-5.5 Pro results are reported separately under a Pro harness, including a 33.2% pass rate. Methods distinguish that setup from the mainline evaluations. The paper supplies no production parameter count or neural architecture; scientific data-generating parameters are unrelated.

sources.title: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.5
sources.evidence: July 29 summary names GPT-5.5 and its lifecycle, says it is not a prior-model fine-tune, and lists April 23 Union-market placement. Its scope reaches the underlying model through the original card relationship, not through an independently named Pro row. Training data quantities and audio/video source material do not establish parameter counts or Pro API modalities.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide explicitly names GPT-5.5 Pro in its model-differences table and gpt-5.5-pro in the extended-retention support list. It explains KV tensors. This binds caching to the exact Pro variant despite its lack of a cached-input discount.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: The archived guide explicitly applies before GPT-5.6 and explains OpenAI caching through Transformer attention key/value projections. Together with the exact Pro caching binding, it supports a qualified broad Transformer inference; it does not disclose full block structure or dense/MoE layout.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses accepts PDF files. For vision-capable models, PDFs are converted to extracted text and page images. Combined with exact Pro vision and Responses support, this establishes PDF as an API input format rather than an additional native sensory modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: April 24, 2026 entry explicitly releases GPT-5.5 Pro for Responses API requests. This follows April 23 ChatGPT availability and does not change the dated April 23 model snapshot.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The complete current document was checked for exact gpt-5.5-pro and its dated identifier; no API shutdown notice was found. This is a documentation observation, not an endpoint availability test.

sources.title: Model Release Notes
sources.evidence: The October 14, 2026 GPT-5.5 product-retirement notice covers ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex and explicitly says API access is unaffected. The notice does not separately enumerate Pro; it is not used to assert an exact Pro API shutdown.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited nonexclusive service/API use and reserve service IP. Combined with hosted distribution, this supports descriptive proprietary licensing, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: Official inventory lists GPT-5.5 Pro as a hosted model and separately lists gpt-oss-120b/20b as Apache-licensed open-weight models. Checked release and model pages offer no downloadable Pro weights.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 API model documentation
sources.evidence: The underlying GPT-5.5 model independently lists prompt_caching. The original system card explicitly relates Pro to that same model; interface/tool capabilities are nevertheless verified from the exact Pro document rather than transferred.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.5 Pro record
sources.evidence: The original catalog lead was accessed through its raw file and checked against primary sources. Its derived-looking 922K input limit is not adopted without an explicit primary limit.

developer.note: Identified by its own release and system card.

family.note: Normalize the GPT-5.5 generation; the original card explicitly identifies Pro as a compute setting of the same underlying model.

release_date.note: Earliest public availability was ChatGPT on April 23; API release followed April 24. The default API snapshot remains dated April 23.

open_weights.note: Checked primary distribution is hosted ChatGPT/API access; no downloadable Pro weights are offered.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-service classification with reserved IP, not an SPDX or downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No numerical total count in the original card, later exact-Pro comparison columns, GeneBench or underlying-model training summary. Targeted first-party parameter/training/interpretability searches found no disclosure. Test-time compute and training-token totals are not parameter counts.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active count or activation topology is disclosed in the bounded original/later sources checked. Parallel test-time computation does not imply MoE or define active weights; total=active is not inferred.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source inference: exact Pro caching support plus the pre-GPT-5.6 Transformer KV explanation establishes a broad Transformer-based classification. The original same-underlying-model relation independently connects Pro to GPT-5.5. Detailed blocks, dense/MoE topology and counts remain undisclosed; no pricing discount is needed for this structural inference.

context_window.note: Exact API total context is 1,050,000 tokens with 128,000 maximum output. Do not derive a separate maximum-input ceiling by subtraction or transfer Codex product limits. No live endpoint test was performed.

modalities.note: Native text/image input and text output. PDF is retained as an API document format converted into text and page images. Hosted image-generation tools and audio/video training data are not native Pro output/input modalities.

reasoning.note: Exact Pro document supports reasoning tokens with medium, high(default) and xhigh effort. Parallel test-time compute is explicitly documented.

tool_call.note: Exact model supports function calling and Responses tools. Batch support is documented. Built-in computer use, tool search, apply_patch and skills are not transferred from GPT-5.5.

Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.5

patch.notes: Released in ChatGPT April 23, 2026; API availability followed April 24. Default API snapshot is gpt-5.5-pro-2026-04-23. Context is 1,050,000 tokens with 128,000 maximum output; reasoning supports medium, high(default) and xhigh. PDF denotes API extraction into text and page images. The system card identifies Pro as the same underlying GPT-5.5 model with parallel test-time compute. Transformer is a qualified broad inference from exact Pro prompt-caching documentation and the pre-GPT-5.6 KV mechanism, corroborated by that model relationship; detailed topology and total/active counts remain undisclosed. The GPT-5.5 October 14 product-retirement notice explicitly excludes API access and does not separately enumerate Pro. No exact Pro API shutdown notice was found; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Confirmed April 23 public release, April 24 API release, exact snapshot, 1.05M context, reasoning, function calling and PDF API-format semantics. Normalize family and proprietary licensing, replace promotional description and add a qualified broad Transformer classification supported by exact Pro caching and the original same-model relation. Total/active counts remain undisclosed after original and later exact-model checks. Product retirement is distinct from API access.
